newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen plans measures to boost B share market.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen plans measures to boost B share market.

text.p: Shenzhen's securities authorities want to boost the position of the city's foreign currency stock market by encouraging more B share secondary listings abroad, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Thursday.
The bourse would also set up a stock data network in Hong Kong to improve B share information flow to investors, the newspaper quoted city official Chen Yingcun as saying.
Chen said the number of secondary listings of Shenzhen-listed B share companies on overseas exchanges should be expanded.
Of the 44 B share companies listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, only China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd currently has a secondary listing abroad, in Singapore.

The exchange is also planning to experiment with more B share issues through public offerings instead of the private placements practised by most companies so far, said Chen after a recent month-long tour abroad to promote Shenzhen's B shares.
Analysts said most Shenzhen-listed B shares have been placed with institutions which tend to hold their shares over the long term, leading to stagnant trading.
"Market liquidity could improve if there were more shares in the hands of individuals," an analyst at J & A Securities said.
City official Chen was also quoted by the newspaper as saying Shenzhen securities authorities should make more promotional visits abroad and focus their efforts on Asia-Pacific countries.
He also called for an increase in the average size of companies to be listed in order to beef up market capitalisation.
Analysts said increasing the scale of the B share market could reduce investment risks.
"Right now, there are too few B share companies listed in Shenzhen, which makes the investment portfolio quite narrow and risky," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
